title: A Teen's Map to Health Care

callouts.label: Trusted Starting Point
callouts.hint: The teen and trusted adult talking on the porch at upper left.
callouts.description: A trusted adult can help identify options, transportation, questions, and support.
callouts.ap_tip: Some teens may begin with another safe support person.

callouts.label: School Support
callouts.hint: The school office with a nurse or counselor in the upper-left center.
callouts.description: School health staff can answer questions, provide support, and connect students with care.
callouts.ap_tip: Services and confidentiality rules vary by school and location.

callouts.label: Primary Care Clinic
callouts.hint: The central clinic with a green medical symbol.
callouts.description: Primary care supports prevention, common health concerns, chronic conditions, and referrals.
callouts.ap_tip: Bring questions and relevant history when possible.

callouts.label: Telehealth
callouts.hint: The private video visit in the upper-right home cutaway.
callouts.description: Telehealth can reduce distance barriers for some kinds of care.
callouts.ap_tip: Privacy, technology, and appropriateness should be considered.

callouts.label: Pharmacy
callouts.hint: The storefront health counter at upper right.
callouts.description: Pharmacists can explain medication use, interactions, storage, and disposal.
callouts.ap_tip: Follow the label and ask when instructions are unclear.

callouts.label: Adolescent and Sexual Health Care
callouts.hint: The colorful welcoming clinic at middle left.
callouts.description: Youth-friendly clinics may offer development, relationship, STI, pregnancy-prevention, and reproductive-health services.
callouts.ap_tip: Available services and consent or confidentiality rules vary by location.

callouts.label: Mental Health Care
callouts.hint: The counselor meeting in the quiet central-right room.
callouts.description: Mental-health professionals support stress, mood, relationships, trauma, and safety concerns.
callouts.ap_tip: Immediate danger or suicide risk requires urgent help.

callouts.label: Transportation
callouts.hint: The accessible bus stop and bus on the right.
callouts.description: Transportation can determine whether a service is truly reachable.
callouts.ap_tip: Plans may include transit, family help, school support, or community programs.

callouts.label: Language Access
callouts.hint: The three-person interpretation conversation in the lower-left room.
callouts.description: Interpreters and communication supports help patients understand and be understood.
callouts.ap_tip: Qualified interpretation protects accuracy and privacy.

callouts.label: Cost and Coverage Support
callouts.hint: The advisor reviewing papers at the lower-middle desk.
callouts.description: Support staff can explain coverage, sliding fees, and assistance programs.
callouts.ap_tip: Ask about costs before care when possible, but emergencies should not wait.

callouts.label: Disability Access
callouts.hint: The wheelchair user approaching the ramped entrance.
callouts.description: Physical, sensory, cognitive, and communication access are part of quality care.
callouts.ap_tip: Patients can request reasonable communication and access supports.

callouts.label: Follow-Up and Navigation
callouts.hint: The reception desk at lower right with a teen and staff member.
callouts.description: Care navigation helps schedule referrals, results, treatment, and follow-up.
callouts.ap_tip: Write down next steps and whom to contact with questions.
